source.title: South Africa's 2024 Grid Emission Factors Report
source.publisher: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Republic of South Africa
source.source_notes: The report uses 2024 calendar-year electricity and emissions data. It states there is an approximately two-year data availability lag. The 2024 factors were published as Government Notice 7891.

unit_conventions.gwp_basis: IPCC Second Assessment Report GWPs were applied in calculation of the reported factors.

factors.name: Domestic Generation Grid Emission Factor
factors.measurement_boundary: GHG emissions per unit of electricity produced within South Africa; domestic generation regardless of whether exported or consumed domestically.
excluded_or_caveats: Not the national end-user electricity consumption factor.
Not a fuel-specific emission factor for a standalone generator.
The methodology excludes domestic generation auxiliary consumption and electricity generated for on-site use from the reported domestic generation denominator.
Do not apply this factor to onsite self-generation as though it were a measured generator-specific lifecycle factor.

factors.name: National Generation Grid Emission Factor
factors.measurement_boundary: GHG emissions associated with end-user electricity consumption; incorporates imported electricity and associated emissions and the treatment of exports, but excludes transmission and distribution losses.
excluded_or_caveats: Use this factor for the declared national consumption boundary, not DGGEF.
Transmission and distribution losses are not included in NGGEF; applicable loss factors may be relevant to Scope 3 reporting.
This is a 2024 calendar-year factor published in 2026, not a real-time 2026 marginal grid factor.

factors.name: Transmission Loss Grid Emission Factor
factors.measurement_boundary: Transmission-loss emissions relative to end-user electricity consumption; includes transmission network energy losses and associated transformer losses.
intended_use: facilities connected directly to transmission network
excluded_or_caveats: Not an alternative to NGGEF for Scope 2.
The report says it is not suitable for onsite self-generation cases where transmission losses are negligible.
Apply only where the reporting boundary requires transmission-loss Scope 3 emissions.

factors.name: Distribution Loss Grid Emission Factor
factors.measurement_boundary: Distribution-loss emissions relative to end-user electricity consumption; includes technical distribution losses and excludes non-technical losses.
excluded_or_caveats: Not an alternative to NGGEF for Scope 2.
The report says it is not suitable for onsite self-generation cases where distribution losses are negligible.
For facilities not fed directly from transmission, the report says both TLGEF and DLGEF should be used for Scope 3 transmission/distribution loss reporting.

supporting_factors.name: Imported Electricity Emission Factor for non-HCB/non-LEC imports
supporting_factors.boundary: SAPP import factor after excluding South Africa, Hidroelectrica de Cahora Bassa (HCB) and Lesotho Electricity Company (LEC) hydropower data.
supporting_factors.use: Supporting calculation for the residual imported electricity source mix; not a national customer factor and not to be substituted for NGGEF.

historical_comparison.interpretation: The DFFE report states all four 2024 factors increased relative to 2023. The NGGEF increased from 0.906 to 0.960 tCO2e/MWh, and DGGEF from 0.942 to 0.994.

modelling_rules: For grid-charged batteries, report location-based electricity consumption emissions using the matched grid consumption boundary and charging losses.

For a site supplied through the distribution network, Scope 2 NGGEF and Scope 3 transmission/distribution loss factors are distinct reporting layers; do not add them unless the selected accounting standard and boundary call for it.
For a site connected directly to transmission, evaluate whether TLGEF applies; DFFE says both TLGEF and DLGEF apply for typical distribution-fed facilities in Scope 3.
For onsite generation, use measured fuel properties, fuel consumption and fuel-specific combustion/upstream factors. Do not use the DGGEF as the onsite engine's emission factor.
Do not compare operational fossil-free status with lifecycle GHG without accounting for charging electricity source, upstream fuel production and equipment lifecycle.
The factor is annual-average location-based accounting data; it is not a marginal dispatch factor, hourly signal, project-specific PPA factor or forward forecast.
Keep the publication year, data year, geographic scope, GWP basis and reporting scope attached to each result.
limitations: The dataset records official published factors; it does not reproduce the complete DFFE methodology or national GHG inventory.
The 2024 factor is the newest official annual factor found for this research snapshot, but the annual publication process may produce later vintages.
Do not use the factors as legal advice or without the applicable reporting standard's rules.
No municipal or subnational grid factors are represented here.
